header:
Fills the rectangle (x0,y0)-(x1,y1), passed as four stacked words x0,y0,x1,y1, with the background colour (word 0x3EFA2): stores them at 0x6CC..0x6D2 and runs bound op 1B (ColorBlit_ByteData) on the 0x6CA block.
Basis: callers + body -- the sound-editor graph routines call it first with their graph box, which their headers describe as 'clears the box'.

header:
XIX = RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A + 0x60 * (s + 1), the 96-byte record of the current patch slot s = (0x34D6) (s >= 30 gives slot 0; signed compare): the XIX twin of AccPatch_GetCurrentSlotAddr, which returns the same address in XIY.
Basis: callers + body -- AccPatch_SetCursorToChannelStart reads a channel's first block word from XIX, AccPatch_ResolveEntryAddr_Helper10_Helper writes the record's +12.. fields through it.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29415 `ld l, (0x34d6:16)` / 29416 `cp l, 0x1e` / 29418 `ld l, 0x0:opc` -- slot index, 30 or more -> 0
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29421 `mul l, 0x60` / 29422 `add hl, 0x60` / 29423 `ld xix, RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A` / 29424 `add xix, xhl` -- 96-byte records from +0x60

sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14374 `ld l, (0x34d6:16)` .. 14382 `ld xiy, RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A` -- AccPatch_GetCurrentSlotAddr computes the same address in XIY (its header, 14368: 'XIY = pointer to patch slot data (at 0x94800 + slot*96 + 96)')
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29476 `calr AccVoice_SetupStyleSlots_Helper2` / 29479 `ld hl, (xix+bc)` -- AccPatch_SetCursorToChannelStart reads the channel's first block number from the record
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29736 `calr AccVoice_SetupStyleSlots_Helper2` / 29737 `ld w, (0x34d8:16)` / 29739 `ld (xix+a), w` -- record +12 written through XIX
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29332 `calr AccVoice_SetupStyleSlots_Helper2` -- AccVoice_SetupStyleSlots, the third caller

why_refused: The body is clear as a mechanism (clears flag 0x0EF6, increments step word 0x0EC4; when it reaches 2*(0x0EC1) it moves to the next of three 32-byte tables 0x0E55/0x0E75/0x0E95 with their counts 0x0E52/0x0E53/0x0E54, or sets 0x0EF6 = 1 after the third), but nothing pins what the steps and the three tables are: the callers are OscScope_UpdateDisplay/OscScope_RefreshLoop and ParamPopup_PartPedal_* blocks with no headers whose names do not fit the code (tick counts divided by 96). A name would be a guess.
evidence: display/scoop_display.s:13963 `ld (3830:16), 0` / 13964 `incw 1, (3780:16)` / 13965 `ld c, (3777:16)` / 13966 `sla c, 1` -- step counter against twice a count
display/scoop_display.s:13976 `ld xde, DisplayStr_BytecodeBlock_A_Tbl` -- selects the next of three sections
display/scoop_display.s:12769 `ld (4372:16), xwa` -- the section pointer is set by PerfMode_ParamHandler_11 code with no header
display/scoop_display.s:13591 `call OscScope_UpdateDisplay_Helper2` / 13573 `div wa, l` -- callers divide a tick count by 96; their names (OscScope) do not describe that

header:
Fat_AllocateClusters(file, zero, count): finds `count` free clusters (Fat_ReadEntry == 0), searching up from the file's cluster word +42 to the volume's cluster limit (vol +54) and then from 2; marks each end-of-chain (vol +36), links it after the previous one (or sets the first cluster +69), and when `zero` is set clears the sectors of the last one. HL = 0, 15 (no free cluster), or 10 / a buffer status on I/O failure.
Basis: callers + body -- the directory walk adds one zeroed cluster when the chain ends, and the file-extend path asks for size / cluster-bytes minus the clusters held.
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5070 `ld wa, (xwa+54)` / 5073 `ld wa, (xwa+42)` / 5075 `ld wa, (xsp+26)` / 5076 `decm 1, (xsp+26)` -- search limit, start cluster and the count argument
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5095 `calr Fat_ReadEntry` -- free-cluster test (Fat_ReadEntry header at 4705)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5125 `ldw hl, 15` -- nothing free: error 15
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5130 `pushm (xwa+36)` / 5131 `pushw iz` / 5134 `calr SeqStep_FileSectorPopReturn` -- writes the FAT entry of the new cluster = end-of-chain value (vol +36)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5137 `cpw (xwa+69), 0` / 5140 `ld (xwa+69), iz` -- first cluster of an empty file
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5179 `cpw (xsp+24), 0` / 5214 `pushw 512` / 5215 `pushw 0` -- the zero flag: Memset 512 bytes per sector of the cluster
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:5967 `cp (xiz+42), wa` / 5972 `pushw 1` / 5973 `pushw 1` / 5975 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper2` -- directory walk: chain ended, add 1 zeroed cluster

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7574 `call Math_DivideU32` / 7578 `sub xhl, xwa` / 7580 `pushw 0` / 7583 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper2` -- SeqChan_TraverseAndProcess: clusters needed minus clusters held (+46), not zeroed

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7645 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper2` / 7660 `pushw SeqChan_ReadNextFromLoop_Str_Dot@hi16` -- SeqChan_ReadNextFromLoop allocates 1 zeroed cluster and then writes the "." entry (it creates a directory)

header:
Fat_GetSectorAtFilePos(file, flags): maps the file's byte position (+22) to its sector (SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper7) and gets that sector's cache buffer with SeqStep_FileIoCheck(flags | 8) into the file's buffer pointer +34. HL = Helper7's error, 10 when no buffer, else the buffer's status word +20.
Basis: callers + body -- the read/write loops and the directory-create path call it before touching sector data; the extend path first sets +22 = size (+71).
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6810 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper7` / 6814 `jr nz, SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Epilogue7` -- position -> sector

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6631 `ld xwa, (xwa+22)` / 6632 `call Math_DivideU32` / 6634 `ld xbc, (xwa+28)` -- Helper7: position / bytes-per-sector (+38) + first sector, for a file with no cluster (+26 = 0)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6815 `ld wa, (xsp+18)` / 6816 `set 3, wa` / 6823 `calr SeqStep_FileIoCheck` / 6825 `ld (xiz+34), xhl` -- buffer for that sector into +34
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6829 `ldw hl, 10` / 6833 `ld hl, (xwa+20)` -- return codes

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7558 `ld xwa, (xwa+71)` / 7559 `ld (xbc+22), xwa` / 7560 `pushw 32` / 7563 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper8` -- SeqChan_TraverseAndProcess: position = size, then the sector there
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7650 `pushw 0` / 7652 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper8` -- SeqChan_ReadNextFromLoop: the new directory's first sector, then (7660) its "." entry

header:
After a floppy sector transfer, handles its error word (*arg1): 0 -> HL = 0. Otherwise counts the attempt (word 0x2271E) and maps the FDC code: 0x2F write-protect -> 31 (HL = 0 at once), 0x30/0x31 -> 32, 0x33/0x35 -> 33, 6 (disk changed) -> 6, other -> 36; re-mounts the volume (SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6) and returns HL = 1 (retry) only if the re-mount succeeded on a 33/6/36 path and 0x2271E is then below 1.
Basis: callers + body -- SeqChan_ByteBlockE (read loop, FDC command 3) and SeqChan_ByteBlockF (write loop, command 4) call it after every transfer and loop while it returns non-zero.
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8241 `calr SeqChan_ByteBlockC` / 8249 `calr SeqChan_ByteBlockD_Helper` / 8252 `jrl nz, SeqChan_ByteBlockD_Helper_Loop` -- SeqChan_ByteBlockE retries while HL != 0
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8361 `calr SeqChan_ByteBlockD` / 8369 `calr SeqChan_ByteBlockD_Helper` / 8372 `jrl nz, SeqChan_ByteBlockD_Helper_Loop3` -- same in SeqChan_ByteBlockF

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8024 `pushw 4` / 8025 `calr SeqStep_ParseVariableHeader` -- SeqChan_ByteBlockD issues FDC command 4 (write sectors; ByteBlockC uses 3 = read), per ../technics-docs/fdc-subsystem.md
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8034 `cpw (xbc), 0` / 8036 `ld hl, 0:i3` -- no error

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8039 `incw 1, (0x2271e:24)` / 8041 `cp wa, 49` / 8043 `cp wa, 48` / 8045 `cp wa, 6:i3` / 8047 `cp wa, 51` / 8049 `cp wa, 53` / 8051 `cp wa, 47` -- FDC codes (docs table: 0x2F write-protected, 0x31 not ready, 0x33 no data, 0x35 missing address mark)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8053 `ldw (xbc), 31` / 8077 `ldw (xbc), 6` -- rewritten codes
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7956 `call FDC_ClearDiskChangeStatus` / 7957 `ld hl, 6:i3` -- code 6 is SeqChan_ByteBlockC's disk-changed result

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8127 `cpw (141086:24), 1` / 8132 `ld hl, (xsp+4)` -- retry only below one counted attempt; 8140 `ldw (0x2271e:24), 0` resets it at the start of each ByteBlockE/F transfer

header:
Loads the value of the part parameter selected by 0x111C (0 PAN, 1 KEY SHIFT, 2 TUNING, 3 BEND SENS) into 0x111D: byte 8 + selector of the parameter block of the part chosen by (0x0D60) through the index table at 0xF1A0 and SubCPU_ToneDispatch (skipped for an absent part, pointer 0xFFFFFFFF).
Basis: callers + body -- both callers set or step the selector 0x111C and then call it before DisplayStr_ShowPartParamLine, which prints 0x111D under that label.
evidence: display/scoop_display.s:12303 `ld (4380:16), 0` / 12304 `call SubCPU_ToneParamDisplay_Helper2` / 12305 `call DisplayStr_ShowPartParamLine` -- SubCPU_ToneParamDisplay opens the pop-up on PAN
display/scoop_display.s:12446 `ld (4380:16), a` / 12447 `call SubCPU_ToneParamDisplay_Helper2` / 12448 `call DisplayStr_ShowPartParamLine` -- SubCPU_ToneParamRet_Target1 steps the selector
display/scoop_display.s:12361 `DisplayStr_ShowPartParamLine: Rebuilds the LCD text line of the part-parameter pop-up` -- (0x111C) picks PAN/KEY SHIFT/TUNING/BEND SENS, (0x111D) is the value
display/scoop_display.s:12343 `ld l, (3424:16)` / 12345 `ld xix, 0xf1a0` / 12348 `ld xix, SubCPU_ToneDispatch` / 12350 `cp xhl, 4294967295` -- the part's parameter block, absent -> skip

display/scoop_display.s:12353 `ld a, (4380:16)` / 12354 `ld xix, SubCPU_ToneParamDisplay_Tbl` / 12356 `ld a, (xhl+wa)` / 12357 `ld (4381:16), a` -- block byte 8 + selector (table 8, 9, 10, 11 at 12432) to 0x111D

why_refused: The body only passes W = 6 * (0xCEF1) and XIY = 0x0D8F to SystemInit_StepHandler_0_Helper2. 0xCEF1 is a chord-note count (ChordTables_TypeNoteCount) and VoiceCtrl_ParamSetupBytecode_Tbl4_Sub fills 0x0D8F with 6-byte note-on records {0x90, channel, note, 64, duration}, but what SystemInit_StepHandler_0_Helper2 / SysEx_BytecodeDispatcher_Tbl2_Helper does with those bytes (it looks like inserting events into a track) is not pinned down, and both named callers (SysEx_BytecodeDispatcher, SystemInit_StepHandler_5) have names that do not describe what they do.
evidence: display/scoop_display.s:9134 `ld b, (0xcef1:16)` / 9139 `ld w, b` / 9140 `ld xiy, 3471` / 9141 `call SystemInit_StepHandler_0_Helper2`
audio/note_voice_mapping.s:16553 `inc 1, (0xcef1:24)` -- 0xCEF1 counts chord notes from ChordTables_TypeNoteCount
display/scoop_display.s:9106 `ld (xiz+0:8), 144` -- the 6-byte records are note-ons; their consumer is undocumented

header:

Basis: callers + body -- five unrelated screen paths call it after changing the selection state; the name follows the tree's X_Wrap convention for one-call forwarders (AccDemo_Init_Wrap).
evidence: display/scoop_display.s:14384 `call Display_UpdateRegion2` / 14385 `ret` -- the whole body

header:
MIDI Reset All Controllers for part (0x9645): posts the control event (0x9644)/(0x9646), then pitch bend 0x4000 (event 0xB1), channel pressure 0 (0xB4), modulation 0 (0xB2), expression 127 (0xB3), voice param 4 = 0x800, re-posts the original event and sets the part's RPN word (0x9674 + 2*part) to the null 0x7F7F.
Basis: callers + body -- MidiCC_Handler_ParamDispatch reaches it through MidiCC_PartTargets_CC121_ResetAll (CC121); the event codes are those of the pitch-bend, channel-pressure, CC1 and CC11 part-target tables.
evidence: midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:903 `ld xix, MidiCC_PartTargets_CC121_ResetAll` / 911 `ld (0x9644:16), bc` / 913 `call VoiceMode3_EvType3_Helper` -- CC121 handler
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:2433 `MidiCC_PartTargets_CC121_ResetAll (+0x6E0): function 40 <- CC121 (reset all`
audio/audio_control_engine.s:11091 `ld e, 177:opc` / 11093 `ldw wa, 0x4000` -- 0xB1 = pitch bend (MidiPB_PartTargets, midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:2462), centre
audio/audio_control_engine.s:11095 `ld e, 180:opc` / 11097 `ldw wa, 0x7f00` -- 0xB4 = channel pressure (MidiCP_PartTargets, 2470), 0
audio/audio_control_engine.s:11099 `ld e, 178:opc` / 11103 `ld e, 179:opc` / 11105 `ldw wa, 0x7f7f` -- 0xB2 = CC1 modulation (2278) -> 0, 0xB3 = CC11 expression (2300) -> 127
audio/audio_control_engine.s:11118 `ld xix, 0x9674` / 11119 `ldw (xix+hl), 0x7f7f` -- RPN word of the part (midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:2478) set to null
audio/audio_control_engine.s:9858 `call VoiceMode3_EvType3_Helper` -- VoiceMode3_EvType3, the second caller, with BC = (0x91B7), DE = 0x7F00

header:
XIZ-preserving wrapper of RhythmVariation_InlineCode_Sub_Helper_Helper, which in mode (0x3712) = 4 steps the note value (0x3714) up (W bit 7 clear) or down within 1..13.
Basis: callers + body -- AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handler03 calls it and redraws the beat block; 0x3714 is the note value that Disp_ShowNoteValueFields names and PerfMode_Evt03_FlagHandler_A also clamps to 1..13.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25127 `push xiz` / 25128 `calr RhythmVariation_InlineCode_Sub_Helper_Helper` / 25129 `pop xiz` -- the body
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25132 `cp (0x3712:16), 4` / 25136 `bit 7, w` / 25138 `inc 1, (0x3714:16)` / 25141 `ld (0x3714:16), 13` -- the stepper (down: min 1)
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:34135 `or (0xe3e2:16), 8` / 34136 `call AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handler03_Helper` -- entry 3 of AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handlers (34040)
display/scoop_display.s:14841 `0x0ED9 <- 3 chars of Tbl_NoteValueNames[((0x3714) & 15) * 4],` -- 0x3714 is the note value
display/scoop_display.s:1207 `ldb_d8 a, (0x3714)` / 1209 `ld h, 13:opc` -- PerfMode_Evt03_FlagHandler_A steps the same byte within 1..13

header:
XIZ-preserving wrapper of RhythmVariation_Select_Helper3, which in mode (0x3712) = 4 steps the articulation (0x3716: TENU/NORM/STAC/CUTT) up (W bit 7 clear) or down within 0..3; in other modes it latches the direction in (0x372D) bit 4 (up) / bit 5 (down).
Basis: callers + body -- AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handler05 calls it; 0x3716 is the articulation index Disp_ShowNoteValueFields names and PerfMode_Evt03_ClampAndUpdate clamps to 0..3.

sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25203 `or (0x372d:16), 16` -- other modes: direction flag
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:34160 `call AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handler05_Helper` -- entry 5 of AccDraw_SecondarySub_Handlers
display/scoop_display.s:14843 `0x0EE3 <- 4 chars of Tbl_ArticulationNames[((0x3716) & 3) * 4]` / 14844 `("TENU"/"NORM"/"STAC"/"CUTT")`

why_refused: Mechanically it moves pattern data backward (lddr) across the linked 256-byte blocks (data bytes 6..0xFF) when offset (0x3660) is above (0x365E), with the two partial lengths in 0x3654/0x3656. Its only caller is a branch of AccPatch_CalcBlockCopySetup, which has no header, and the roles of 0x365E/0x3660/0x3658 (source/destination offsets? which entry?) are not documented, so whether this opens a gap (insert) or shifts after a delete cannot be told from callers.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:18136 `calr AccPatch_CalcBlockCopy_Clamp_Helper` -- only caller, a branch of AccPatch_CalcBlockCopySetup
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:18155 `ld wa, (0x3660:16)` / 18156 `sub wa, (0x365e:16)` / 18169 `calr DSP_BlockCopyReverse`

header:
Stores the pattern-data cursor (block word 0x3612, offset word 0x3614) as entry C (0..7) of the measure-start table: RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A + 0xC40 + 160*slot(0x34D6) + 32*channelIndex + 4*C, channelIndex from the one-hot channel (0x379B) through the byte table AccPatch_SlotScanByteData_Code.
Basis: callers + body -- AccPatch_SlotScanByteData fills entries 0..7 with the channel start; the AccPatch_CheckAndInitDemo_Helper loop stores the cursor after skipping each measure (one beats-per-measure run of 0x81 beat codes); AccVoice_BarCounterBytecodeData_Helper/_Helper2 read +0/+2 back.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14163 `ld a, 160:opc` / 14164 `ld c, (0x34d6:16)` / 14173 `mul de, 32` / 14175 `add xwa, 3136` / 14176 `add xwa, RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A` -- the address
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14179 `sll c, 2` / 14180 `ld wa, (0x3612:16)` / 14181 `ld (xix+c), wa` / 14182 `ld wa, (0x3614:16)` / 14184 `ld (xix+c), wa` -- the cursor pair
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14102 `ld (0x3612:16), hl` / 14103 `ldw (0x3614:16), 6` -- AccPatch_InitCurrentSlotPointer: cursor = channel start (block, first data byte 6)
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14109 `cp c, 8` / 14112 `calr AccPatch_CheckAndInitDemo_Helper4` -- AccPatch_SlotScanByteData: entries 0..7
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14085 `calr AccPatch_CheckAndInitDemo_Helper3` / 14088 `calr AccPatch_CheckAndInitDemo_Helper4` -- skip one measure, store entry C
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14140 `ld a, (xiy+12)` / 14141 `add xwa, AccTone_LookupByProgram_Table` / 14143 `ld c, (xiy+13)` -- beats per measure and measure count of the slot
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:12299 `add xbc, 611392` -- 611392 = 0x95440 = RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A + 0xC40, the reader's base
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14187 `push sr` .. 14191 `normal` -- AccPatch_SlotScanByteData_Code is a byte table (02 03 04 00 01 00 ...) spelled as instructions

header:

evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:15863 `ld xiy, RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A` / 15867 `cp a, 72` / 15870 `cp a, 0:i3` / 15873 `cp a, 75` -- 'H', 0, 'K'
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:15877 `call AccDemo_Init_Wrap` -- otherwise rebuild
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:11651 `ld xiy, Demo_StyleRhythmData` / 11652 `ld xix, RHYTHM_PATTERN_BUF_A` / 11654 `ldw bc, 0x60` -- AccDemo_LoadRhythm (from AccDemo_Init) copies the image header
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:11809 `.byte 0x48, 0x00, 0x4b, 0x00` -- the default image starts with that header
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:13866 `calr AccPatch_MultiCallWrapper_Helper` / 13867 `calr AccPatch_ClearModeFlag` -- AccPatch_MultiCallWrapper
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:12093 `bit 5, (0xbd1a:16)` / 12100 `call AccPatch_MultiCallWrapper` -- reached after a SysEx block (MidiSysEx_ProcessBlock_Helper8)

header:
Fills the header of the current patch slot record (XIX from AccVoice_SetupStyleSlots_Helper2): +12 = time-signature code (0x34D8), +13 = last measure index (0x34D7), +14 = 32, +15 = 0, +16/+17 = bytes from the tables at 0x38D2/0x38D9 for the drum-channel index, and the 16-character name "Easy" at +64.
Basis: callers + body -- AccVoice_SetupSlots_Apply (the slot setup whose comment lists it) calls it; AccPatch_CheckAndInitDemo_Helper2 reads +12 as the beats-per-measure index and +13 + 1 as the measure count.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29731 `calr AccPatch_ResolveEntryAddr_Helper10_Helper` -- AccVoice_SetupSlots_Apply
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29737 `ld w, (0x34d8:16)` / 29739 `ld (xix+a), w` / 29740 `ld w, (13527:16)` -- +12 and +13 (13527 = 0x34D7)
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29743 `ld w, 32:opc` / 29746 `ld w, 0:opc` -- +14, +15
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29754 `ld xiy, 0x38d2` / 29758 `ld xiy, 14553` -- +16, +17 per drum channel
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29762 `ld xiy, AccVoice_SlotName_Easy` / 29763 `add xix, 64` -- the name "Easy" at +64
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14140 `ld a, (xiy+12)` / 14143 `ld c, (xiy+13)` / 14144 `inc 1, c` -- readers of +12/+13
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:14792 `ld l, (0x34d8:16)` / 14796 `ld (0x34d9:16), a` -- 0x34D8 indexes the beats-per-measure table (AccPatch_ReadVoiceStride)

why_refused: It loops over measures 0..(0x34D7) (counter 0x38D1), and for each one runs Helper4 (Helper5 records a per-measure entry and starts a new block; Helper6 copies events beat by beat from the slot stream pointer at 0x3898 + 4*drum), then terminates with Helper10 (end code 0x83). But Helper5 stores through XWA = 4*measure (a low address, not the 0x380A table it computed), the source streams in 0x3898 are not documented, and the caller AccVoice_SetupSlots_DataBlock has no header -- naming it 'copy measures' would rest on a guess about the data source.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29486 `ld c, (0x34d7:16)` / 29492 `calr AccPatch_ResolveEntryAddr_Helper4`
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:29452 `calr AccPatch_ResolveEntryAddr_Helper3` -- only caller AccVoice_SetupSlots_DataBlock

header:
Averages the new tap tempo WA with the previous one or two (words 0x3492, 0x3494; 0 = none) and posts the result as the tempo event (E = 0x48, D = 8) through SwbtWr_TrailingBytecode.
Basis: callers + body -- AccProcess_InlinedCode times successive presses (SWBTWR_PAYLOAD_1 = 18, pressed) with SYSTEM_TIMESTAMP, clamps the interval to 100..750 and passes WA = 30000 / interval; SeqTimer_PostTempoUpdate posts tempo with the same E/D.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:10413 `cp a, 18` / 10422 `ld wa, (SYSTEM_TIMESTAMP:16)` -- the caller times a panel event

sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:10439 `cp wa, 750` / 10443 `cp wa, 100` / 10448 `ld xwa, 0x7530` / 10449 `div xwa, bc` / 10451 `calr AccProcess_Entry_Helper` -- interval clamped, WA = 30000 / interval
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:10463 `ld de, (0x3492:16)` / 10464 `ld bc, (0x3494:16)` / 10472 `srl wa, 1` / 10478 `div wa, 3` -- mean of 1, 2 or 3 values
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:10480 `ld e, 72:opc` / 10481 `ld d, 8:opc` / 10482 `call SwbtWr_TrailingBytecode`
ui/ui_playback_modes.s:143 `ld e, 0x48:opc` / 144 `ld d, 0x8:opc` -- SeqTimer_PostTempoUpdate posts the tempo word with the same event

why_refused: It maps the index byte 0x32D8 through AccTuning_ReadAndApplyOffset_Table into 0x342B and through the byte table pointed to by 0x32CE into 0x342A (0xFF -> raw `.byte 0x81, 0x19, 0x2a, 0x34` then 0x342B = 0). 0x342A ends up as the slot index the callers use for RhythmTiming_OffsetTable, but what 0x32D8 selects, what the two tables mean and what 0x342B is are not documented, and all callers (AccTone_InlineBytecodeData, AccTone_JumpTableData_*) carry placeholder names.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:12237 `ld a, (13016:16)` / 12239 `lda xbc, (AccTuning_ReadAndApplyOffset_Table:24)` / 12241 `ld (13355:16), a`
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:12248 `.byte 0x81, 0x19, 0x2a, 0x34` -- still a raw encoding

why_refused: When (0x32E5) >= 240 it runs AccTone_InlineBytecodeData_Code_Helper (refused above) and, if the resulting 0x342A differs from 0x3421, executes the raw `.byte 0xf1, 0x3b, 0x33, 0xb8` (a bit set on 0x333B). Its meaning depends on the unnamed lookup and on what 0x333B flags, and the caller AccTone_JumpTableData is a placeholder.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:12400 `cp (13029:16), 240` / 12402 `calr AccTone_InlineBytecodeData_Code_Helper` / 12406 `.byte 0xf1, 0x3b, 0x33, 0xb8`
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:13796 `call AccTone_JumpTableData_Helper2` -- only caller

header:
Draw-task body of a plain dotted line: from point (XWA) to point (XBC) (each {x, y} words) in colour DE, writing straight into OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1 (320-byte rows) with a 2-on / 3-off pattern (counter 0,1 draw; 2,3 skip; 4 resets), horizontal, vertical and fixed-point sloped cases; ends with SetChangeRect. No draw-mode dispatch, unlike DrawDottedLineWithMode_Impl.
Basis: callers + body -- DrawDesignBox_ByteData (the standard direct-or-DrawQueue_Alloc wrapper; misnamed, and itself unreferenced) and its queued record function DrawDesignBox_ByteData_Code call it.

ui/ui_window_procs.s:4002 `calr DrawQueue_Alloc` / 4004 `lda xbc, (DrawDesignBox_ByteData_Code:24)` -- otherwise queued (same idiom as DrawLine/DrawBox)
ui/ui_window_procs.s:4023 `lda xhl, (xwa+4)` / 4024 `lda xbc, (xwa+8)` / 4025 `ld de, (xwa+12)` / 4029 `calr ClampColorToRange_Helper` -- the queued call: two points and a colour

header:
